# sego sesearch query matrix.
#
# One case per line, tab separated.  Lines starting with '#' and blank lines are
# ignored.  Fields, in order:
#
#   1  case name          also the file name stem of expected/<case>.txt
#                         (matches [A-Za-z0-9_.-]+)
#   2  policy fixture     path relative to the repository root, e.g.
#                         testdata/policies/sego_test-v32.pol
#   3  arguments          the exact argv, arguments only (no program name),
#                         separated by single spaces; no argument contains a
#                         space, so a plain split on ' ' recovers the argv
#   4  expected exit code present only for cases whose exit status is not 0
#                         (the only such case is no_ruletype, exit 2)
#
# A line therefore has exactly 3 tabs-separated fields, or 4 when the exit code
# is not 0, e.g.
#
#   allow_all<TAB>testdata/policies/sego_test-v32.pol<TAB>--allow
#   no_ruletype<TAB>testdata/policies/sego_test-v32.pol<TAB>-s app_t<TAB>2
#
# expected/<case>.txt holds the exact stdout of the reference tool for that
# argv, byte for byte, including the trailing newline.  A case that matches
# nothing has an existing but empty (0 byte) expected file; the cases that are
# deliberately empty are listed in expected/README.md.
#
# Provenance of the golden outputs (see expected/README.md for the full story):
#
#   * 74 of the 103 cases are recorded from the reference oracle
#     /usr/bin/sesearch (setools 4.2.2).  For that oracle the 4.8 spelling of
#     two options is translated when the CLI does not accept it:
#     --role_transition -> --role_trans, --range_transition -> --range_trans
#     (-T exists in both).  The translation is a pure rename; gen_expected.sh
#     does it for the 4.2.2 runs.
#   * 29 cases are recorded from the setools 4.8 CLI (built from the in-tree
#     setools; see expected/README.md) because 4.2.2 cannot express the argv
#     (-Sp) or cannot read the fixture (-v33/-v35, sego_nlmsg, extra_cond_xperm):
#     + the three "-Sp" cases -- the flag is 4.8 only, the 4.2.2 library
#       implements the same perms_subset semantics but has no switch for it;
#     + the -v33/-v35, sego_nlmsg (libsepol 3.0 cannot decode nlmsg extended
#       permissions at all) and extra_cond_xperm (conditional extended
#       permissions, policy version 34+) cases -- 4.2.2 stops at version 32;
#     + seven cases that 4.2.2 *can* run but prints differently: complete ioctl
#       driver ranges (0x0000-0x00ff) are printed as "0x0000" and do not match
#       "-x 0x0000-0x00ff -ex" there, and the corpus is kept consistent with the
#       4.8 CLI.  exact list: allowxperm_all, allow_and_allowxperm,
#       te_xperm_ruletypes, te_mixed_ruletypes, xperm_ioctl_driver_range,
#       xperm_ioctl_driver_range_exact, xperm_ioctl_driver_range_v30;
#     + the two legacy_neverallow* cases, whose point is the 4.8 usage error.
#   * the two "legacy_neverallow*" cases use the --neverallow/--neverallowxperm
#     flags that exist in setools 4.2.2 but were removed from the 4.8 CLI.  They
#     assert 4.8 CLI parity: the invocation must fail with the argparse usage
#     error, i.e. exit status 2 and empty stdout (the usage text goes to stderr,
#     which is not part of the golden).  Their recorded exit status therefore
#     comes from the 4.8 oracle, not from 4.2.2, which still accepts the flags
#     and exits 0.
#
# Regenerate the goldens with testdata/gen_expected.sh (see expected/README.md).
#
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# rule types, one flag at a time, -A, and combinations
allow_all	testdata/policies/sego_test-v32.pol	--allow
allowxperm_all	testdata/policies/sego_test-v32.pol	--allowxperm
auditallow_all	testdata/policies/sego_test-v32.pol	--auditallow
auditallowxperm_all	testdata/policies/sego_test-v32.pol	--auditallowxperm
dontaudit_all	testdata/policies/sego_test-v32.pol	--dontaudit
dontauditxperm_all	testdata/policies/sego_test-v32.pol	--dontauditxperm
type_trans_all	testdata/policies/sego_test-v32.pol	-T
type_change_all	testdata/policies/sego_test-v32.pol	--type_change
type_member_all	testdata/policies/sego_test-v32.pol	--type_member
role_allow_all	testdata/policies/sego_test-v32.pol	--role_allow
role_transition_all	testdata/policies/sego_test-v32.pol	--role_transition
range_transition_all	testdata/policies/sego_test-v32.pol	--range_transition
allow_and_allowxperm	testdata/policies/sego_test-v32.pol	-A
te_plain_ruletypes	testdata/policies/sego_test-v32.pol	--allow --auditallow --dontaudit
te_xperm_ruletypes	testdata/policies/sego_test-v32.pol	--allowxperm --auditallowxperm --dontauditxperm
te_mixed_ruletypes	testdata/policies/sego_test-v32.pol	--allow --allowxperm --dontauditxperm
# neverallow/neverallowxperm: the rules are assertions and never reach the
# binary policy.  neverallow_absent_* look for exactly the rule/permission the
# neverallow rules forbid and must match nothing (exit 0; both oracles agree).
# The two legacy_* cases use the --neverallow/--neverallowxperm flags, which
# setools 4.8 removed: their argv must fail as a usage error (exit 2, empty
# stdout, usage on stderr), which is the 4.8 CLI parity assertion recorded from
# the 4.8 oracle.
neverallow_absent_te	testdata/policies/sego_test-v32.pol	--allow -s plain_t -t config_t -c file -p read
neverallow_absent_xperm	testdata/policies/sego_test-v32.pol	--allowxperm -s plain_t -t data_t -c chr_file -x 0x1234
legacy_neverallow_te	testdata/policies/sego_test-v32.pol	--neverallow	2
legacy_neverallowxperm_te	testdata/policies/sego_test-v32.pol	--neverallowxperm	2

allow_tgt_attr_indirect	testdata/policies/sego_test-v32.pol	--allow -t special_attr
allow_tgt_attr_direct	testdata/policies/sego_test-v32.pol	--allow -t special_attr -dt
allow_src_attr_tgt_concrete	testdata/policies/sego_test-v32.pol	--allow -s special_attr -t data_t
allow_src_regex	testdata/policies/sego_test-v32.pol	--allow -s .*_t -rs
